item.title: Welcome to Software Beirut
item.description:
Last week, when it briefly looked like the world was collapsing while I sat on the tarmac, I wrote about the arrival of Software Beirut —“where nothing is broken all the time, but anything might break at any time, and the main skill you need is not being surprised.” I’m no Tom Friedman , but many people seemed to enjoy the phrase and encouraged me to keep using it even as outages at the FAA, Chase, and Microsoft proved to be isolated incidents unrelated to bad guys using advanced AI. Well, hold my mustache wax! Because I’m doubling down. The fact that all of the software chaos appears to have had boring causes doesn’t negate my point—it improves it.
